policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'bound him' requires an object pronoun in English whether or not the Greek expresses αὐτόν after δήσας; the wording does not distinguish presence from omission.
'put him in prison' renders all three: the Greek article on φυλακῇ is not carried by English 'in prison', and ἀπέθετο/ἔθετο and the word order are indistinguishable in the ASV.
ASV 'John said unto him' renders the dative αὐτῷ, excluding r02 which lacks it; the order of αὐτῷ and ὁ Ἰωάννης is not distinguished in English.
ASV 'when Herod's birthday came' renders the aorist γενομένοις ('having come'); RP's Γενεσίων ἀγομένων would be 'when the birthday feast was being kept/celebrated', which the ASV does not say.
ἐάν and ἄν are orthographic variants of the same particle in this construction; 'whatsoever she should ask' renders either.

ASV has the finite main verb and an adversative: 'And the king was grieved; but for the sake of his oaths' — ἐλυπήθη ὁ βασιλεύς, διὰ δὲ. The base participle λυπηθείς would give a subordinate 'And the king, being grieved, ... commanded'.
The article before the proper name Ἰωάννην is not rendered in English; 'beheaded John' is identical either way.
ASV 'took up the corpse' renders πτῶμα; RP σῶμα would be 'the body', which is how the ASV renders σῶμα elsewhere.
ASV 'buried him' renders masculine αὐτόν; the neuter αὐτό, agreeing with πτῶμα/σῶμα, would be 'buried it'.
ASV opens 'Now when Jesus heard it', rendering the postpositive δέ; RP's Καὶ ἀκούσας would give 'And when Jesus heard it', the rendering the ASV uses for καί elsewhere in this chapter.
ASV 'And he came forth' has the pronoun only; the RP addition ὁ Ἰησοῦς would give the named subject 'Jesus came forth'.
ASV reads 'the disciples came to him', not 'his disciples'; the RP addition αὐτοῦ is unrendered and not supplied in italics.
'Bring them hither to me' contains both αὐτούς and ὧδε; the Greek order of the two is not recoverable from the English.
ASV 'on the grass' uses an English mass noun that renders the Greek singular τοῦ χόρτου and the plural τοὺς χόρτους alike.
ASV 'straightway he constrained the disciples' names no subject; the RP addition ὁ Ἰησοῦς would give 'Jesus constrained'.
The article τό before πέραν is not rendered separately; 'unto the other side' is the same English with or without it.

The ASV text reads 'the boat was now in the midst of the sea' = μέσον τῆς θαλάσσης ἦν, and the mapped textual_variant note assigns the base reading to the margin: 'Some ancient authorities read was many furlongs distant from the land.'

'he came unto them' renders either the simplex ἦλθεν or the compound ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτούς, which is idiomatically 'came to them'; the ASV carries no separate word for the ἀπο- prefix but does not exclude it.
ASV 'he came unto them, walking upon the sea' leaves the subject pronominal; the RP addition ὁ Ἰησοῦς would name Jesus here, as the ASV does at v.27 where the Greek has the name.
ASV 'upon the sea' renders ἐπί with the accusative or the genitive alike; the case is not distinguished in English.
'And when the disciples saw him' fits both the δέ clause with fronted οἱ μαθηταί and the καί clause with the subject following; the ASV renders both connectives 'And' and does not show Greek order.
ASV 'walking on the sea' renders ἐπί with either case; genitive and accusative are indistinguishable in the English.
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are equivalent forms of the same adverb; the ASV 'straightway' renders either.
'Jesus spake unto them' contains both ὁ Ἰησοῦς and αὐτοῖς; English word order is fixed by the verb and does not reflect the Greek order.
'Peter answered him and said' includes αὐτῷ, ὁ Πέτρος and εἶπεν in all readings; only their Greek order differs, which the English does not show.
'bid me come unto thee' renders ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σέ in either order; the variant is order alone.
The article added before Πέτρος is not rendered in English; 'Peter went down from the boat' is unchanged either way.
ASV reads 'walked upon the waters to come to Jesus', the infinitive of purpose ἐλθεῖν; the mapped textual_variant note puts the base καὶ ἦλθεν in the margin: 'Some ancient authorities read and came.'
ASV text reads 'when he saw the wind' with no adjective, and the mapped textual_variant note treats ἰσχυρόν as an addition of other witnesses: 'Many ancient authorities add strong.'
ASV 'when they were gone up into the boat' renders ἀναβάντων ('having gone up'); RP ἐμβάντων would be 'when they were entered into the boat'.
ASV 'they that were in the boat worshipped him' has a single finite verb; the RP/Treg participle ἐλθόντες would add 'came and worshipped', which the ASV does not have.
ASV 'they came to the land, unto Gennesaret' renders two prepositional phrases, ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν and εἰς Γεννησαρέτ; RP's single εἰς τὴν γῆν Γεννησαρέτ would be 'to the land of Gennesaret'.
